title: My Dad Said My Games Made Me Lazy on Our Chore Chart #shorts

cast.dad: a stick-figure father with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, short brown hair and a green sweater
cast.girl: a stick-figure girl with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, two black pigtails and a yellow hoodie
cast.max: a small stick-figure boy with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, messy orange hair and a red t-shirt

lines.text: Dad said gaming made me lazy on our chore chart, so who really worked harder?
lines.label: hook
lines.headline: who really worked harder
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, short brown hair and green sweater, standing in a kitchen pointing angrily at exactly one plain white paper grid chart whose boxes hold only colored checkmarks, a blank empty white strip along its top edge, the only chart in the picture, taped on the fridge, frowning, mouth open talking, evening light

lines.text: On Sunday's fridge chart, my brother Max finished ten of twelve chores; I finished eight.
lines.label: the score
lines.headline: Max ten, me eight
lines.image: {girl} is the only person in the picture, two black pigtails and yellow hoodie, standing in a kitchen staring up at exactly one plain white paper grid chart whose boxes hold only colored checkmarks, a blank empty white strip along its top edge, the only chart in the picture, taped on the fridge, one row of checkmarks longer than the other, worried face, morning light

lines.text: Dad said Max is only seven and beats me anyway, so games made me lazy.
lines.label: the charge
lines.headline: games made me lazy
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, short brown hair and green sweater, standing in a kitchen with arms crossed, stern face, mouth open talking, exactly one plain white paper grid chart whose boxes hold only colored checkmarks, a blank empty white strip along its top edge, the only chart in the picture taped on the fridge behind him

lines.text: He locked my console in his closet until I beat Max on the chart.
lines.label: locked away
lines.headline: console locked away
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, short brown hair and green sweater, in a hallway putting exactly one small flat black game console box on a high closet shelf and turning a small key in the closet door, stern face, no TV in the picture

lines.text: Next Sunday I worked harder, lost ten to eight again, and Dad took my phone.
lines.label: worse
lines.headline: lost again, phone gone
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, short brown hair and green sweater, standing in a kitchen holding exactly one phone up high out of reach, frowning, exactly one plain white paper grid chart whose boxes hold only colored checkmarks, a blank empty white strip along its top edge, the only chart in the picture taped on the fridge behind him, evening

lines.text: I cried alone at the kitchen table, staring at that unfair chart on the fridge.
lines.label: tears
lines.headline: crying at the table
lines.image: close-up of {girl}, the only person in the picture, two black pigtails and yellow hoodie, sitting alone at a kitchen table, a single tear running down her cheek, sad eyes, dim evening kitchen

lines.text: But my games never compare hard-mode scores with easy-mode scores, so I split the chart.
lines.label: gamer clue
lines.headline: split the chart
lines.image: {girl} is the only person in the picture, two black pigtails and yellow hoodie, sitting at a kitchen table holding a black marker and drawing one thick straight black line from top to bottom down the middle of exactly one plain white paper grid chart whose boxes hold only colored checkmarks, a blank empty white strip along its top edge, the only chart in the picture, the line clearly cutting the chart into a left half and a right half, determined face, lamp light

lines.text: Dishes were hard mode: I finished six of ten nights, Max just one of two.
lines.label: hard mode
lines.headline: dishes are hard mode
lines.image: {girl} is the only person in the picture, two black pigtails and yellow hoodie, standing on a step stool at a kitchen sink washing a tall stack of dirty plates and pots, sleeves rolled up, tired but proud face, night

lines.text: Feeding the dog was easy mode: I finished two of two, Max nine of ten.
lines.label: easy mode
lines.headline: dog is easy mode
lines.image: {max} is the only person in the picture, messy orange hair and red t-shirt, pouring dry food into exactly one dog bowl on a kitchen floor, exactly one small brown dog wagging its tail beside the bowl, happy face, morning

lines.text: Dad gave me ten dish nights because Max is seven, so Max got easy mode.
lines.label: the twist
lines.headline: Dad gave me hard mode
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, short brown hair and green sweater, standing at a kitchen sink stacking a tall pile of dirty plates and pots on the counter, cheerful face, exactly one small dog bowl on the floor across the kitchen, the only dog bowl in the picture, night

lines.text: I showed Dad I won both modes, and only lost because I got hard mode.
lines.label: proof
lines.headline: won both modes
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, short brown hair and green sweater, sitting at a kitchen table reading exactly one plain white paper grid chart whose boxes hold only colored checkmarks, a blank empty white strip along its top edge, the only chart in the picture with a black line drawn down its middle, stunned face, mouth open, eyebrows raised

lines.text: Console back, but Dad still says I'm lazy, and I say I'm on hard mode.
lines.label: the ending
lines.headline: console back
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, short brown hair and green sweater, standing in a living room with arms crossed and a grumpy smile, exactly one small flat black game console box back on a shelf behind him, the only console in the picture, no TV in the picture
